registers.name: SREG
registers.title: Status Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x3f

fields.name: I
fields.text: 1 lets interrupts run, each still gated by its own enable bit; 0 blocks all of them. Hardware clears it when an interrupt is taken and RETI sets it again; SEI sets it and CLI clears it.

fields.name: T
fields.text: One-bit store for the bit copy instructions: BST moves a register bit into T, and BLD moves T into a register bit.

fields.name: H
fields.text: Half carry flag, set by some arithmetic operations; of use in BCD arithmetic.

fields.name: S
fields.text: Sign: always N exclusive-ORed with V.

fields.name: V
fields.text: Two's complement overflow flag, used in two's complement arithmetic.

fields.name: N
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is negative.

fields.name: Z
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic result is zero.

fields.name: C
fields.text: Set when an arithmetic or logic operation produces a carry.

fields.name: SPn

registers.name: EEAR
registers.title: EEPROM Address Register Low and High Byte
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x21
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0xXX.

fields.name: EEARn
fields.text: Bit n of the EEPROM byte address, counted linearly from 0 to 1023 across the 512B/1K/2K EEPROM. Undefined after reset; load a valid address before any EEPROM access.

registers.name: EEDR
registers.title: EEPROM Data Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x20

fields.name: EEDR
fields.text: Byte to store at the EEAR address on an EEPROM write; on a read, it receives the byte found at that address.

registers.name: EECR
registers.title: EEPROM Control Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x1f
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x00.

fields.name: EEPMn
fields.text: Bit n of the programming mode that a write of EEPE starts: 00 erase then write as one atomic step (3.4ms), 01 erase alone (1.8ms), 10 write alone (1.8ms), 11 reserved. Writes are ignored while EEPE is 1. Reset returns them to 00 unless programming is in progress.

rows: Erase then write, one atomic step.

fields.name: EERIE
fields.text: 1 turns on the EEPROM Ready interrupt, provided SREG.I is 1; 0 turns it off. The interrupt fires continuously while EEPE is 0, and never during an EEPROM write or SPM.

fields.name: EEMPE
fields.text: Arms EEPE: with EEMPE at 1, a write of EEPE to 1 inside the next four clock cycles stores the data at the chosen EEPROM address; with EEMPE at 0, writing EEPE has no effect. Hardware returns EEMPE to 0 four clock cycles after software sets it.

fields.name: EEPE
fields.text: Writing 1 starts the EEPROM write of EEDR to EEAR; EEMPE must be written to 1 first, in a separate write, and EEPE set within four clock cycles of it, or nothing is written. Sequence: wait for EEPE = 0, wait for SPMCSR.SPMEN = 0 (needed only when a boot loader programs Flash), optionally load EEAR and EEDR, write EEMPE = 1 with EEPE = 0, then EEPE = 1. No EEPROM write can happen while the CPU writes Flash. An interrupt between the last two steps makes the write fail, and an interrupt routine that uses the EEPROM corrupts an access it interrupts; keeping global interrupts off through the sequence avoids both. Hardware clears EEPE when the write finishes (typically 3.3ms, 26,368 calibrated RC oscillator cycles). The CPU stops for two cycles after EEPE is set.

fields.name: EERE
fields.text: Writing 1 reads the EEPROM byte at EEAR into EEDR at once, within one instruction; the CPU then stops for four cycles. No read and no change to EEAR is possible while a write runs, so check EEPE first. EEPROM timing comes from the calibrated RC oscillator.

fields.name: CALn
fields.text: Bit n of the trim for the calibrated internal RC oscillator. Reset loads the factory value; software may write another to change the frequency, though outside the specified range results are not guaranteed. This oscillator times EEPROM and Flash writes, so trimming it changes their timing; do not go above 8.8MHz when writing EEPROM or Flash, or the write may fail. CAL7 picks the range, 0 the lower and 1 the upper, and the ranges overlap (0x7F runs faster than 0x80). CAL[6:0] sets the frequency within the range, 0x00 lowest to 0x7F highest.

registers.name: PLLCSR
registers.title: PLL Control and Status Register
notes: The register's reset value is also given as 0x0.

fields.name: PLLF
fields.text: Selects the PLL division factor, and so its output frequency.

fields.name: PLLE
fields.text: 1 starts the PLL, and starts the internal RC oscillator as its reference if it is not running. Reads 1 whenever the PLL is the system clock source.

fields.name: PLOCK
fields.text: 1 when the PLL has locked to its reference, after which CLKPLL may be enabled for the fast peripherals. Lock takes about 100ms from enabling the PLL.

fields.name: CLKPCE
fields.text: Must be set to 1 before CLKPS can be changed; the write only takes effect if the other CLKPR bits are written 0 in the same write. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write or when CLKPS is written; writing it again inside those four cycles neither restarts nor clears the count.

fields.name: CLKPSn
fields.text: Bit n of the divider between the selected clock source and the system clock; may be changed while running, and slows every synchronous peripheral along with the CPU. 0000 /1, 0001 /2, 0010 /4, 0011 /8, 0100 /16, 0101 /32, 0110 /64, 0111 /128, 1000 /256, 1001 to 1111 reserved. Reset value comes from the CKDIV8 fuse: 0000 when unprogrammed, 0011 (divide by 8) when programmed; parts ship with CKDIV8 programmed. Any value can be written whatever CKDIV8 is; software must pick a division large enough when the clock source is faster than the device may run under present conditions.

registers.name: SMCR
registers.title: Sleep Mode Control Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x33

fields.name: SM2
fields.text: Top bit of SM[2:0], which picks the sleep mode: Idle at 000, ADC Noise Reduction at 001, Power-down at 010, Standby at 110; every other code is reserved. Standby is recommended only for use with an external (unnamed) source.

fields.name: SM1
fields.text: Middle bit of SM[2:0], the sleep mode chosen with SM2.

fields.name: SM0
fields.text: Low bit of SM[2:0], the sleep mode chosen with SM2.

fields.name: SE
fields.text: 1 lets the SLEEP instruction put the MCU into the selected sleep mode. Setting it just before SLEEP and clearing it on wake-up keeps the MCU from sleeping by accident.

fields.name: PRCAN
fields.text: 1 stops the CAN controller's clock to save power. Re-initialize the CAN after turning it back on.

fields.name: PRPSC
fields.text: 1 stops the PSC's clock to save power. Re-initialize the PSC after turning it back on.

fields.name: PRTIM1
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter1; once enabled again it carries on as it was before.

fields.name: PRTIM0
fields.text: 1 shuts down Timer/Counter0; once enabled again it carries on as it was before.

fields.name: PRSPI
fields.text: 1 stops the SPI's clock, shutting it down; re-initialize the SPI after turning it back on. Leave at 0 when debugWIRE on-chip debug is in use.

fields.name: PRLIN
fields.text: 1 stops the LIN controller's clock to save power. Re-initialize the LIN controller after turning it back on.

fields.name: PRADC
fields.text: 1 shuts down the ADC, which must be disabled first. While the ADC is off, the analog comparator has no access to the ADC input multiplexer.

registers.name: MCUSR
registers.title: MCU Status Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x34

fields.name: WDRF
fields.text: Set by a watchdog system reset. A power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: BORF
fields.text: Set by a brown-out reset. A power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: EXTRF
fields.text: Set by an external reset. A power-on reset clears it, as does a write of 0.

fields.name: PORF
fields.text: Set by a power-on reset. Cleared only by writing 0.

fields.name: WDIF
fields.text: Set on a watchdog timeout when the watchdog is set up to interrupt. Cleared by hardware when the interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1. With SREG.I and WDIE both 1, the timeout interrupt runs.

fields.name: WDIE
fields.text: 1 enables the watchdog interrupt, provided SREG.I is 1. With WDE = 0 the watchdog is in Interrupt mode: a timeout runs the interrupt. With WDE = 1 it runs in the combined interrupt-then-reset mode: an initial timeout sets WDIF, and running the vector clears WDIE and WDIF in hardware, leaving System Reset mode; WDIE must be set again after each interrupt, not from inside the interrupt routine, and a timeout before the interrupt runs resets the system. Modes by WDTON, WDE, WDIE: 1,0,0 stopped; 1,0,1 interrupt; 1,1,0 reset; 1,1,1 interrupt then reset mode; WDTON = 0 (programmed) always reset.

fields.name: WDP[3]
fields.text: Watchdog timer prescaler, bit 3.

fields.name: WDCE
fields.text: Must be 1 to clear WDE or change the prescaler bits, in a timed sequence. Hardware clears it four clock cycles after it is written to 1.

fields.name: WDE
fields.text: Enables the watchdog system reset. MCUSR.WDRF forces it to 1, so WDRF must be cleared before WDE can be cleared; this keeps resets coming while a fault lasts and gives a safe start after it.

fields.name: SPIPS
fields.text: Chooses which pins carry the SPI. The programming port is always on the alternate SPI pins.

values.text: SPI on MISO, MOSI, SCK and SS.
SPI on the alternate pins MISO_A, MOSI_A, SCK_A, SS_A.

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: 1 turns off the pull-ups on all I/O ports, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn ask for one ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01).

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: 0 puts the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash; 1 moves them to the start of the boot loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it, write IVCE = 1, then within four cycles write the new IVSEL with IVCE = 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction following the IVSEL write, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; SREG.I is left as it was. With the vectors in the boot section and boot lock bit BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while code runs from the application section; with the vectors in the application section and BLB12 programmed, interrupts are off while code runs from the boot section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Must be written to 1 before IVSEL can be changed. Hardware clears it four cycles later or when IVSEL is written. Setting it turns interrupts off for the IVSEL change sequence.

fields.name: ISC3n
fields.text: Bit n of the condition on pin INT3 that raises external interrupt 3, which runs when SREG.I and its mask bit are 1. The pin is sampled before edges are found: an edge or toggle pulse longer than one clock period always interrupts, a shorter one may not; a low level must last until the current instruction finishes.

fields.name: ISC2n
fields.text: Bit n of the condition on pin INT2 that raises external interrupt 2, which runs when SREG.I and its mask bit are 1. fields.name: ISC1n

The pin is sampled before edges are found: an edge or toggle pulse longer than one clock period always interrupts, a shorter one may not; a low level must last until the current instruction finishes.

fields.name: ISC0n
fields.text: Bit n of the condition on pin INT0 that raises external interrupt 0, which runs when SREG.I and its mask bit are 1. The pin is sampled before edges are found: an edge or toggle pulse longer than one clock period always interrupts, a shorter one may not; a low level must last until the current instruction finishes.

fields.name: TOV
fields.text: Goes to 1 on a Timer/Counter0 overflow; when it is set depends on WGM0[2:0]. Cleared by hardware when its interrupt vector runs, or by writing 1 to it. The overflow interrupt runs when this flag, TOIE0 and the SREG I-bit are all set.

fields.name: COM1
fields.text: COM1A[1:0] and COM1B[1:0] set how pins OC1A and OC1B behave; any nonzero pair takes its pin from the port function, and the pin's DDR bit must be 1 for the output to drive. The meaning depends on WGM1[3:0]. In fast PWM, when OCR1A/OCR1B equals TOP and COM1A1/COM1B1 is 1, the match is ignored and the set or clear happens at BOTTOM. Both phase-correct PWM modes also treat OCR1A/OCR1B equal to TOP with COM1A1/COM1B1 set as a special case.

fields.name: WGM11
fields.text: Bit 1 of WGM1[3:0], which with TCCR1B.WGM1[3:2] chooses the counting sequence, TOP source and waveform. Modes (WGM1 value: mode, TOP, OCR1x update, TOV1 set at): 0 normal, 0xFFFF, immediate, MAX; 1 phase correct 8-bit, 0x00FF, TOP, BOTTOM; 2 phase correct 9-bit, 0x01FF, TOP, BOTTOM; 3 phase correct 10-bit, 0x03FF, TOP, BOTTOM; 4 CTC, OCR1A, immediate, MAX; 5 fast PWM 8-bit, 0x00FF, BOTTOM, TOP; 6 fast PWM 9-bit, 0x01FF, BOTTOM, TOP; 7 fast PWM 10-bit, 0x03FF, BOTTOM, TOP; 8 phase and frequency correct, ICR1, BOTTOM, BOTTOM; 9 phase and frequency correct, OCR1A, BOTTOM, BOTTOM; 10 phase correct, ICR1, TOP, BOTTOM; 11 phase correct, OCR1A, TOP, BOTTOM; 12 CTC, ICR1, immediate, MAX; 13 reserved; 14 fast PWM with ICR1 as TOP, update and TOV1 as mode 15; 15 fast PWM, OCR1A, BOTTOM, TOP. fields.name: WGM10

fields.name: ICES1

fields.name: WGM13

fields.name: WGM12

fields.name: PPRE

fields.name: PCLKSEL

fields.name: PAOCm

fields.name: PRFMm

registers.title: MCU Control Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x35

fields.name: SPIPS
fields.text: Moves the SPI signals between the main and the alternate SPI pins. The programming port always stays on the alternate SPI pins.

values.text: SPI on MISO, MOSI, SCK and SS.
SPI on the alternate pins (the _A versions of MISO, MOSI, SCK, SS).

fields.name: PUD
fields.text: Writing 1 turns off every I/O port pull-up, even on pins whose DDxn and PORTxn ask for one ({DDxn, PORTxn} = 0b01).

fields.name: IVSEL
fields.text: 0 places the interrupt vectors at the start of Flash; 1 moves them to the start of the Boot Loader section, whose address the BOOTSZ fuses set. To change it: write IVCE to 1, then within four cycles write the new IVSEL value with IVCE 0. Interrupts are off from the cycle IVCE is set until after the instruction that follows the IVSEL write, or for four cycles if IVSEL is not written; the SREG I-bit is not touched. With the vectors in the Boot Loader section and BLB02 programmed, interrupts are off while running from the Application section; with the vectors in the Application section and BLB12 programmed, they are off while running from the Boot Loader section.

fields.name: IVCE
fields.text: Write 1 to allow a change of IVSEL; this also turns interrupts off for the change sequence. Hardware clears it four cycles after the write, or when IVSEL is written.

registers.name: SPCR0
registers.title: SPI Control Register 0
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x2c

fields.name: SPIE0
fields.text: When 1, the SPI interrupt runs whenever SPSR.SPIF is set and the SREG global interrupt bit is set.

fields.name: SPE0
fields.text: Writing 1 enables the SPI; it must be 1 for any SPI operation.

fields.name: DORD0
fields.text: 1 sends the LSB of each data word first; 0 sends the MSB first.

fields.name: MSTR0
fields.text: 1 selects SPI master mode, 0 slave mode. If SS is an input and is pulled low while MSTR is 1, hardware clears MSTR and sets SPSR.SPIF; MSTR must then be set again to return to master mode.

fields.name: CPOL0
fields.text: 1 makes SCK idle high (leading edge falling, trailing edge rising); 0 makes it idle low (leading edge rising, trailing edge falling).

fields.name: CPHA0
fields.text: Chooses the SCK edge that samples data: 0 samples on the leading edge and sets up on the trailing edge; 1 sets up on the leading edge and samples on the trailing edge.

fields.name: SPR0n
fields.text: Set the SCK rate in master mode and do nothing in slave mode. With SPI2X:SPR01:SPR00: SCK = fosc divided by 4 (000), 16 (001), 64 (010), 128 (011), 2 (100), 8 (101), 32 (110), 64 (111).

registers.name: SPSR0
registers.title: SPI Status Register 0
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x2d

fields.name: SPIF0
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a serial transfer completes, and also when SS is an input pulled low in master mode; raises an interrupt if SPCR.SPIE and global interrupts are enabled. Cleared by hardware when its interrupt vector runs, or by reading SPSR with SPIF set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: WCOL0
fields.text: Goes to 1 when SPDR is written while a transfer is in progress. It and SPIF are cleared by reading SPSR with WCOL set and then accessing SPDR.

fields.name: SPI2X0
fields.text: Writing 1 doubles SCK in master mode, so the shortest SCK period is two CPU clocks. As a slave the SPI is only guaranteed up to fosc/4. The SPI interface also serves to download and upload program memory and EEPROM.

registers.name: SPDR0
registers.title: SPI Data Register 0
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x2e

fields.name: SPID
fields.text: Data byte moved to and from the SPI shift register: writing it starts sending, reading it returns the received byte from the shift register's buffer.

fields.name: ABRQ
fields.text: Requests an abort of CAN activity; the bit does not clear itself.

values.text: Abort: CANEN1 and CANEN2 are cleared, pending communications are disabled at once and the one in progress finishes normally with its status flags set; CANCDMOB is left unchanged.

fields.name: OVRQ
fields.text: Requests an overload frame; the bit does not clear itself, and OVFG in CANGSTA shows the overload frame going out.

values.text: An overload frame is sent after the next frame received.

fields.name: TTC
fields.text: Selects time trigger communication.

fields.name: SYNTTC
fields.text: Picks the point where the TTC timer is captured; used in TTC mode only.

values.text: Captured on the last bit of EOF.

fields.name: LISTEN
fields.text: Selects listening mode.

fields.name: TEST
fields.text: Selects test mode, meant for factory testing rather than customer use; the CAN may malfunction while it is set.

fields.name: ENA/STB
fields.text: Commands enable or standby; the command takes effect later, so ENFG in CANGSTA shows the actual mode. 1 = enable: the channel enters enable mode after reading 11 recessive bits. Entering standby during a reception may corrupt that reception or leave the controller in a wrong state, from which SWRES restarts it correctly; otherwise wait for RXBSY to clear before standby, or better, issue ABRQ first and then wait for RXBSY to clear. CAN bus integrity is not affected either way.

values.text: Standby: a transmission in progress finishes normally, then the channel freezes (no MOb's CONMOB bits change) and the transmitter holds the bus recessive; the receiver is off, but every register and the mailbox stay readable and writable by the CPU.

fields.name: SWRES
fields.text: Resets the CAN controller alone; the bit clears itself.

values.text: Reset, combined by OR with the hardware reset.

fields.name: OVRG
fields.text: Shows an overload frame being sent; raises no interrupt.

values.text: Set by hardware for as long as the overload frame is being sent.

fields.name: TXBSY
fields.text: Shows the transmitter busy; raises no interrupt.

values.text: Set by hardware while a data, remote, overload or error frame, an ACK field or an inter-frame space is being sent.

fields.name: RXBSY
fields.text: Shows the receiver busy; raises no interrupt.

values.text: Set by hardware while a frame is being received or monitored.

fields.name: ENFG
fields.text: Shows whether the CAN controller is actually enabled, since an enable/standby command takes effect later; raises no interrupt.

fields.name: BOFF
fields.text: Shows whether the CAN channel is in bus off mode; only the entry into bus off raises the BOFFIT interrupt.

fields.name: ERRP
fields.text: Shows whether the CAN channel is in error passive mode; raises no interrupt.

fields.name: CANIT
fields.text: Read-only summary of every CAN controller interrupt except OVRTIM; usable for polling.

fields.name: BOFFIT
fields.text: Set only when the CAN goes into bus off mode from error passive mode; cleared by writing 1.

values.text: The CAN has entered bus off mode.

fields.name: OVRTIM
fields.text: CAN timer overrun flag; cleared by writing 1 or by entering the CAN timer overrun interrupt handler.

values.text: Set when the CAN timer rolls over from 0xFFFF to 0.

fields.name: BXOK
fields.text: Frame buffer receive flag; cleared by writing 1, which works only after the CONMOB fields of all the buffer's MObs have been written again.

values.text: The frame buffer receive has finished.

fields.name: SERG
fields.text: General stuff error flag; cleared by writing 1.

values.text: More than 5 bits in a row of the same polarity were seen.

fields.name: CERG
fields.text: General CRC error flag; cleared by writing 1.

values.text: The CRC computed over the destuffed message does not match the CRC field.

fields.name: FERG
fields.text: General form error flag; cleared by writing 1.

values.text: The fixed form of the CRC delimiter, acknowledgment delimiter or EOF was broken one or more times.

fields.name: AERG
fields.text: General acknowledgment error flag; cleared by writing 1.

values.text: No dominant bit was seen in the acknowledge slot.

fields.name: ENIT
fields.text: Enables the CAN interrupts as a whole, the CAN timer overrun interrupt excepted.

fields.name: ENBOFF
fields.text: Enables the bus off interrupt.

fields.name: ENRX
fields.text: Enables the receive interrupt.

fields.name: ENTX
fields.text: Enables the transmit interrupt.

fields.name: ENERR

fields.name: BRPn

fields.name: SJWn
fields.text: Resynchronization jump width: the largest number of clock cycles a resynchronization may add to or remove from a bit period when the controller resynchronizes on a signal edge to make up for phase shifts between the oscillators of different bus nodes; Tsjw = Tscl x (SJW[1:0] + 1).

fields.name: PRSn
fields.text: Propagation time segment: the part of the bit time that makes up for physical delays in the network, equal to twice the sum of bus line propagation, input comparator delay and output driver delay; Tprs = Tscl x (PRS[2:0] + 1).

fields.name: PHS2n
fields.text: Phase segment 2, which makes up for phase edge errors and may be shortened by the resynchronization jump width; PHS2[2:0] must be at least 1 and no more than PHS1[2:0]; Tphs2 = Tscl x (PHS2[2:0] + 1).

fields.name: PHS1n
fields.text: Phase segment 1, which makes up for phase edge errors and may be lengthened by the resynchronization jump width; Tphs1 = Tscl x (PHS1[2:0] + 1).

fields.name: SMP
fields.text: Selects one or three samples per bit, to filter noise on the TxCAN input pin; SMP must be 0 when BRP[5:0] = 0, because TQ then equals TclkIO.

values.text: One sample, at the configured sample point SP.

fields.name: RXOK
fields.text: Set when the reception enabled for the MOb has finished, once the 6th EOF bit ends; can raise an interrupt and is cleared by a read-modify-write of the whole CANSTMOB. When a frame matches several MObs, the lowest MOb index (0 to 14) is updated first.

fields.text: Bit error, in transmission only: the bit read back differs from the bit sent, except for a recessive bit sent and read dominant during arbitration and for a dominant acknowledge slot read while sending an error frame. fields.name: SERR
fields.text: Stuff error: more than five bits in a row of the same polarity. Can raise an interrupt; cleared by a read-modify-write of the whole CANSTMOB.

fields.name: CERR

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Form error: the fixed form of the CRC delimiter, acknowledgment delimiter or EOF was broken one or more times. Can raise an interrupt; cleared by a read-modify-write of the whole CANSTMOB.

fields.name: AERR
fields.text: Acknowledgment error: no dominant bit was seen in the acknowledge slot. Can raise an interrupt; cleared by a read-modify-write of the whole CANSTMOB.

fields.text: Chooses which change of the comparator 1 output raises its interrupt.

fields.name: AC1ICE
fields.text: 1 routes the analog comparator 1 event to the Timer/Counter1 input capture front end, so it uses that unit's noise canceler and edge select; TIMSK1.ICIE1 must be set for it to raise the input capture interrupt. With ICES1=1 the AC1O rising edge is the capture event, with ICES1=0 the falling edge. 0 removes the link between comparator and input capture.

registers.name: DACON
registers.title: Digital to Analog Conversion Control Register

fields.name: DAATE
fields.text: 1 makes the DAC take a new input value on the rising edge of the trigger chosen by DATS; 0 makes it take the new value whenever DACH is written.

fields.name: DATS
fields.text: Picks the event whose rising flag edge updates the DAC input when DAATE is set, whether or not that interrupt is enabled.

fields.name: DALA
fields.text: 1 left-adjusts the DAC input data in its registers, 0 right-adjusts it; a change reaches the output at the next DACH write.

fields.name: DAOE
fields.text: 1 drives the DAC output onto the D2A pin; 0 keeps the DAC for internal use.

fields.name: DAEN
fields.text: 1 turns the DAC on; 0 turns it off.

registers.name: DAC
registers.title: Digital to Analog Converter input Register

fields.name: DACn
fields.text: The 10-bit value the DAC turns into a voltage; writing DACL holds the update until DACH is written, so DACL goes first.

property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x31

fields.name: DWDR
fields.text: A channel from the running program to the debugger, reachable only through debugWIRE, so it is not a general purpose register in normal use.

registers.name: SPMCSR
registers.title: Store Program Memory Control and Status Register
property: when addressing as i/o register: address offset is 0x37

fields.name: SPMIE
fields.text: 1, with the SREG I-bit set, turns on the SPM ready interrupt, which keeps running as long as SPMEN is 0.

fields.name: RWWSB
fields.text: Set by hardware when a self-programming erase or write of the RWW section begins; while set, the RWW section cannot be read. Cleared by writing RWWSRE to 1 after the operation finishes, or by starting a page load.

fields.name: SIGRD
fields.text: Written to 1 together with SPMEN, makes an LPM within three clock cycles read a signature row byte into the destination register; an SPM within four cycles after then does nothing. Reserved for future use; not to be used.

fields.name: RWWSRE
fields.text: While the RWW section is being erased or written it cannot be read (RWWSB set). Once SPMEN has cleared, writing RWWSRE to 1 with SPMEN makes the next SPM within four clock cycles open the RWW section again. It cannot be reopened while SPMEN is set; writing it during a Flash load aborts the load and loses the data.

fields.name: BLBSET
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles set the boot lock and memory lock bits from R0, ignoring R1 and the Z-pointer; clears itself when done or after four cycles with no SPM. An LPM issued no more than three cycles after both bits are written reads the lock bits or the fuse bits, chosen by Z0, into the destination register.

fields.name: PGWRT
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles write the temporary buffer to the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer, ignoring R1 and R0; clears itself when done or after four cycles with no SPM. The CPU halts for the whole write when the page is in the NRWW section.

fields.name: PGERS
fields.text: Written to 1 with SPMEN, makes the next SPM within four clock cycles erase the page addressed by the high part of the Z-pointer, ignoring R1 and R0; clears itself when done or after four cycles with no SPM. The CPU halts for the whole operation when the page is in the NRWW section.

fields.name: SPMEN
fields.text: Lets an SPM run during the four clock cycles that follow. Written with RWWSRE, BLBSET, PGWRT or PGERS, the SPM does that bit's operation; written alone, the SPM stores R1:R0 in the temporary page buffer at the Z-pointer address, its LSB ignored. Clears itself after the SPM or after four cycles without one, but stays 1 until a page erase or page write ends. Only 10001, 01001, 00101, 00011 or 00001 in the low five bits has any effect.
